prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 3: swap family off gbdt entirely and onto a bagged, highly-randomised ensemble — extra_trees — with the preprocessing block otherwise held as close to comparable as the family allows. Two hist_gbdt points now bracket the boosting space and both plateau at balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut ≈0.78 (KS ≈0.57), and cut_headroom 0.0083 says the operating point is spent, so the only axis left is the ranking. extra_trees is the family furthest from boosted stumps in how it builds a ranking: fully-grown randomised trees averaged over many bootstraps produce a smoother, higher-resolution probability ranking on wide, noisy tabular data (119 features, 180 one-hot levels, many weakly-informative columns) than 300 depth-3 boosted trees can. Config: n_estimators 600, max_depth 20, min_samples_leaf 5, class_weight 'balanced_subsample'-equivalent via class_weight 'balanced' to hold recall≈specificity where hist_gbdt's balanced cut landed near centre (recall 0.768 / specificity 0.785). Because extra_trees cannot split on NaN, preprocessing moves to impute: median with scale: false (trees are scale-insensitive), and I add missing_count as the one missingness column a non-NaN-splitting family cannot recover from a median-imputed matrix — several columns carry heavy missingness (worst 0.7852, 60 columns affected) and how many of a row's fields were recorded is a single cheap column rather than 119 indicators. Read roc_auc against 0.8583 and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against 0.7849: if the randomised-bagging ranking also lands near 0.78 at best cut, then two structurally different families agree the feature set caps KS near 0.57, the 0.8882 bar is not reachable from these columns, and the remaining attempts should be spent confirming the best ranking (e.g. a large random_forest or an mlp on scaled inputs) rather than on more operating-point moves.",
  "model_family": "bagging",
  "candidate_models": [
    "extra_trees",
    "random_forest",
    "mlp"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 600,
    "max_depth": 20,
    "min_samples_leaf": 5,
    "class_weight": "balanced"
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": true
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Family changes from gbdt (hist_gbdt, both prior attempts) to bagging (extra_trees) — a different ranking generator, not another point in the boosting space. Preprocessing changes from impute: none to impute: median (extra_trees cannot split on NaN, so the executor would force median anyway) and adds missing_count, a single aggregate column standing in for the missingness the previous NaN-splitting fits could express natively. Hyperparameters are the bagging family's own (n_estimators 600, max_depth 20, min_samples_leaf 5) rather than boosting's learning_rate<path> schedule; class_weight stays 'balanced' so the cut sits near where it did and the roc_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut movement is attributable to the family swap.",
  "rationale": "The Critic's verdict is wrong_model_family and the arithmetic supports spending on the ranking axis only: shortfall 0.1116, cut_headroom 0.0083 (7% of it), KS 0.5698 versus the 0.7764 the bar demands. class_weight and scale_pos_weight move the operating point, which is exhausted; more hist_gbdt points moved best-cut by 0.0039. xgboost is the Critic's suggestion but it is the same gbdt family and the same shrink-a-boosted-ensemble mechanism that has now plateaued twice, so it is the weaker test of whether the ranking can move at all. extra_trees is a genuinely different induction scheme — deep, randomly-split, averaged trees — and is noted as often better with noisy labels, which fits a target where the strongest single predictor ('like', strong corr) is surrounded by ~100 near-zero-corr columns. Cost 4 with 5,026 training rows and 600 trees fits comfortably inside 600s and 2GB (hist_gbdt took 6s). I am not claiming this reaches 0.8882 — the recorded family-swap span on the ranking axis is 0.0022–0.0077 roc_auc, far under the 0.1116 needed — but it is the largest untried move available to this executor, and its result is decisive information for the remaining two attempts: either the ranking moves materially or two structurally different families jointly establish that the bar sits above what these columns support.",
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "feature_engineering"
  ],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 3
}
